content.user_title: Choose the Right Frontend UI Library
content.value_statement: Choosing among frontend libraries can waste time and create inconsistent dependencies. This skill maps a defined UI task to an opinionated, curated library recommendation.
actual_capabilities: Matches component tasks to libraries for accessible primitives, command menus, toasts, OTP inputs, and control panels.
Recommends focused libraries for animation, animated numbers, text effects, globes, dynamic images, and syntax highlighting.
Distinguishes streaming charts from general dashboard charts.
Selects tools for drag and drop, list virtualization, state, conditional classes, variants, and theme switching.
Checks existing project dependencies before recommending a change.
Explains when a task falls outside the curated list.
limitations: Uses an opinionated list and does not compare every available library.
Does not verify current package versions, maintenance status, licenses, or vulnerabilities.
Requires project context to determine whether an existing dependency should remain.
Installation and integration happen only when the user requests implementation.

use_cases.title: Select a component library
use_cases.description: Choose an accessible library for dialogs, command menus, notifications, or verification inputs.

use_cases.title: Plan dashboard dependencies
use_cases.description: Match charting, virtualization, state, and theme requirements to focused libraries.

use_cases.title: Review a UI implementation
use_cases.description: Identify custom UI patterns that a curated library can replace more reliably.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a toast library
prompt_templates.prompt: I need toast notifications in a React application. Recommend one library from the curated list and explain the choice in one sentence.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a direct recommendation for one UI task.

prompt_templates.title: Select list virtualization
prompt_templates.prompt: My React page renders more than 1,000 rows. Check the dependencies I provide and recommend the curated solution without replacing suitable installed tools.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer needs a performance library that fits an existing project.

prompt_templates.title: Plan dashboard libraries
prompt_templates.prompt: Map my live chart, drag and drop, shared state, and dark mode requirements to the curated libraries. Explain each boundary briefly.
prompt_templates.scenario: A technical lead is planning several related frontend capabilities.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a UI dependency plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my frontend plan and package.json. Identify mismatched dependencies, preserve suitable choices, and recommend justified changes from the curated list. Do not modify files.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user wants a dependency review with explicit change control.

output_examples.input: I need an accessible dropdown and dialog without built-in styling.
output_examples.output: Use base-ui. It provides unstyled accessible primitives with focus management and dismissal behavior.

output_examples.input: Our dashboard receives data continuously and the chart scrolls over time.
output_examples.output: Use Liveline for real-time streaming charts. Use Recharts when the data is static or updated as a general dashboard.

output_examples.input: We need conditional classes for a button with typed size and intent variants.
output_examples.output: Use cva for typed variants. Use clsx only when the conditions are ad hoc and do not define a component variant API.

best_practices: Describe the UI behavior, accessibility needs, data scale, and update frequency.
Share existing dependencies so the recommendation can avoid unnecessary package changes.
Request installation separately when you want the skill to modify a project.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a broad list when one task has a clear curated choice.
Do not replace a working competitor without considering migration cost.
Do not treat recommendations as security, licensing, or maintenance approval.

faq.question: Which frontend tasks does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers UI primitives, motion, charts, drag and drop, virtualization, state management, styling helpers, and theme switching.

faq.question: Will it recommend libraries outside the curated list?
faq.answer: Yes, when the task is not covered. The response will clearly identify that the recommendation comes from general knowledge.

faq.question: Does it inspect existing dependencies?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide project context or package.json so it can preserve suitable installed libraries.

faq.question: Does it install the recommended package?
faq.answer: Only when installation or implementation is part of the request.

faq.question: Does a recommendation confirm package security?
faq.answer: No. Review current advisories, package versions, licenses, maintenance status, and organizational policies before adoption.

faq.question: Can it compare several competing libraries?
faq.answer: The default behavior recommends one curated option. Ask explicitly for alternatives when comparison is required.
